query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small fraction of aluminum (e.g., ~3 at%) to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a protective Al2O3 surface scale at high temperatures, significantly reducing oxygen uptake without compromising the alloy’s ductility or high-temperature strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the as-cast condition
generation.intervention: Doping with ~3 at% Al by vacuum arc-melting or induction melting with aluminum addition
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 1000 °C for up to 100 hours under tensile loads up to the alloy’s yield strength (~500 MPa at 1000 °C)
generation.structural_mediator: Al-doped oxide scale (Al2O3) formed on the surface
generation.mechanism: During high-temperature exposure in air, the doped alloy forms a stable, slow-growing alumina scale that hinders oxygen diffusion, maintaining the underlying alloy’s mechanical integrity
generation.predicted_outcome: Oxygen ingress is reduced by at least 50%, preserving more than 80% of the alloy’s original tensile ductility and yield strength at 1000 °C relative to undoped cast HfNbTaTiZr
generation.baseline: Undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits limited oxygen resistance, leading to rapid embrittlement and reduced high-temperature ductility
generation.boundary: Intervention remains effective up to 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 100 hours, with tensile loads not exceeding ~500 MPa; higher temperatures or longer exposures require further verification
generation.uncertainty: Exact Al content and its influence on phase stability and long-term creep performance are not fully established

falsification_experiment.design: Compare cast HfNbTaTiZr vs. identical alloy doped with ~3 at% Al by conducting isothermal oxidation tests at 1000 °C in air under tensile load
measurements: Weight change due to oxide scale formation over time
Microstructural examination (scanning electron microscopy) for oxide scale characterization
Tensile ductility and yield strength pre- and post-exposure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-doped alloy exhibits oxygen uptake comparable to or exceeding that of the undoped alloy, or suffers the same degree of loss in ductility and strength after exposure at 1000 °C, the hypothesis is falsified.
